title: Shadowing
concept: Shadowing lets you declare a new variable with the same name as an existing one, hiding the original in the current scope.
why: Shadowing is useful for transforming values without inventing awkward temporary names like 'x2' or 'result2'.
tips: Each `let x = ...` creates a NEW variable with the same name
Shadowing can change the type — `let x = 5; let x = "five";` works!
Old variable still exists but is inaccessible while shadowed
In a new block scope, shadowing ends when the block ends
common_mistakes: Excessive shadowing that makes code confusing to follow
Thinking shadowing modifies the old variable — it creates a new one
